question: What is the primary goal of occupational health hazard control in clinical and industrial environments?

options.A: To increase overall facility productivity regardless of worker safety
options.B: To create a hazard-free working environment by eliminating or minimizing exposure risks
options.C: To replace the need for clinical nursing education and training
options.D: To solely focus on treating injuries after they have already occurred

explanation: The primary goal of occupational health hazard control is to systematically identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks to create a safe working environment and prevent injuries or illnesses before they happen. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Which of the following represents a biological hazard commonly encountered by nurses in Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Heavy computer monitors causing eye strain
options.B: Infectious pathogens such as Lassa fever or HIV
options.D: Loud noises from hospital standby generators

explanation: Biological hazards involve infectious agents and pathogens like Lassa fever or HIV that nurses may be exposed to during patient care and clinical procedures. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: According to the hierarchy of hazard controls, which intervention is considered the most effective?
explanation: Elimination sits at the very top of the hierarchy of hazard controls, making it the most effective measure because it physically removes the hazard from the workplace entirely. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) placed at the bottom of the hierarchy of hazard controls?

options.A: It is completely useless in clinical settings
options.B: It relies heavily on human behavior and leaves the hazard present in the environment
options.C: It is the most expensive method to implement
options.D: It requires physical modification of the building structure

explanation: PPE is at the bottom because the hazard is still present, and it depends heavily on proper worker compliance and fitting to provide protection, making it less reliable than elimination or engineering controls. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h2)

question: Which of the following is a classic nursing example of substitution in occupational health?

options.A: Replacing latex gloves with nitrile gloves to prevent allergies
options.B: Requiring all nurses to wear face shields during surgery
options.C: Scheduling mandatory safety meetings every month
options.D: Writing a new hospital policy on hand hygiene

explanation: Replacing latex gloves with nitrile gloves is a clear example of substitution, where a hazardous material causing allergies is replaced with a safer alternative. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary difference between elimination and substitution?

options.A: Elimination removes the hazard completely, while substitution replaces it with a less hazardous alternative
options.B: Substitution is always more expensive than elimination
options.C: Elimination relies on PPE, while substitution uses administrative rules
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms

explanation: Elimination means getting rid of the hazard entirely, whereas substitution involves swapping a dangerous element for one that is less hazardous. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary advantage of engineering controls over administrative controls or PPE?

options.A: They are always the cheapest option available
options.B: They do not rely heavily on human behavior or constant worker compliance
options.C: They completely eliminate all workplace hazards instantly
options.D: They replace the need for any nursing safety education

explanation: Engineering controls physically isolate the worker from the hazard, making them highly reliable because they do not depend on the worker remembering to use them correctly every single time. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: What is the specific function of a negative pressure isolation room in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To prevent contaminated air from escaping into hospital corridors
options.B: To safely incinerate biohazardous medical waste
options.C: To provide ergonomic support for nurses lifting heavy patients
options.D: To eliminate the need for handwashing stations

explanation: Negative pressure rooms are engineering controls designed to keep airborne pathogens contained by ensuring air flows inward, preventing contaminated air from spreading to other hospital areas. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an administrative control in a hospital?

options.A: Installing a mechanical patient lift in every room
options.B: Implementing a strict policy prohibiting the recapping of used needles
options.C: Completely banning the use of all chemical disinfectants
options.D: Providing N95 respirators for infectious disease wards

explanation: Prohibiting the recapping of used needles is an administrative policy and work practice designed to reduce the risk of needlestick injuries among healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: How do administrative controls primarily protect healthcare workers?

options.A: By physically removing the hazard from the hospital building
options.B: By altering work schedules, enforcing safety policies, and providing safety training
options.C: By creating a chemical barrier on the surface of the skin
options.D: By substituting dangerous equipment with digital alternatives

explanation: Administrative controls work by changing work practices, setting up schedules, enforcing policies, and training staff to minimize their time and exposure to hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h5)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) considered the last line of defense in occupational safety?

options.A: It is the most expensive and complex control measure to purchase
options.B: The hazard remains present in the environment, and PPE relies entirely on correct usage by the worker
options.C: It is designed to completely eliminate workplace hazards at their source
options.D: It replaces the need for engineering and administrative controls entirely

explanation: PPE is the last line of defense because the hazard is still present, and failure in worker compliance or equipment integrity can directly result in exposure and injury. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: What critical action must a nurse perform immediately after removing contaminated personal protective equipment?

options.A: Complete an incident report for the shift
options.C: Put on a second set of sterile gloves
options.D: Sanitize the patient's room with bleach

explanation: Performing hand hygiene immediately after doffing PPE is essential to remove any potential pathogens that may have transferred to the hands during the removal process. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting periodic medical surveillance for healthcare workers?

options.A: To punish staff members who fail to follow hospital safety rules
options.B: To detect early signs of work-related illness or exposure and initiate timely interventions
options.C: To replace the need for environmental hazard controls in the hospital
options.D: To determine the monthly salary scale for nursing staff

explanation: Medical surveillance helps identify early health changes or occupational exposures (such as tuberculosis screening) so that workers can receive prompt treatment and preventive care. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of environmental monitoring in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Administering a questionnaire on nursing job satisfaction
options.B: Using a dosimeter badge to measure radiation exposure in the radiology department
options.C: Conducting a physical head-to-toe assessment of an admitted patient
options.D: Reviewing patient vital signs charts on the ward

explanation: Using dosimeter badges to measure radiation levels in radiology is a direct form of environmental and workplace monitoring to ensure safety limits are not exceeded. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned to manage and lead occupational health hazard control programs?

options.A: They have exclusive authority to purchase hospital building materials
options.B: They combine clinical expertise with public health knowledge to assess workers and environments
options.C: They are exempt from encountering workplace hazards themselves
options.D: They manage the financial budgets of all healthcare institutions

explanation: Nurses possess a unique blend of clinical skills and public health understanding, enabling them to effectively evaluate both individual worker health and broader environmental risks. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)

question: In the context of Nigerian community health nursing, what is an important responsibility regarding informal sector workers?

options.A: Firing workers who do not comply with factory regulations
options.B: Educating laborers and traders on safety practices, ergonomics, and protective gear
options.C: Operating heavy industrial machinery to demonstrate safety
options.D: Designing architectural blueprints for new factories

explanation: Community health nurses extend their expertise to informal workers by providing education on ergonomics, safety measures, and protective equipment to prevent injuries in non-traditional work settings. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)
